pairs.question: Falce minax et parte tua maiore, Priape, ad fontem, quaeso, dic mihi qua sit iter.
pairs.answer: Vade per has vites, quarum si carpseris uvam, cur aliter sumas, hospes, habebis aquam.
pairs.derivation: A traveller's whole speech is a request for directions to the spring (dic mihi qua sit iter); Priapus answers with the route (vade per has vites...). Stripped section marker [XXX] and the quotation marks around the speech. Kept the traveller's utterance contiguous including quaeso. Answer is Priapus' full two-line reply, which directly gives the way.

pairs.question: Cur pictum memori sit in tabella membrum, unde procreamur?
pairs.answer: Cum penis mihi forte laesus esset chirurgique manum miser timerem, dis me legitimis nimisque magnis, ut Phoebo puta filioque Phoebi, curatum dare mentulam verebar.
pairs.derivation: Speaker poses readers' question why the member is depicted on a votive tablet, then answers it himself. Dropped the framing verb quaeritis ('you ask'), which narrates the asking, leaving 'Cur pictum memori sit in tabella membrum, unde procreamur?' contiguous. Answer cut at the semicolon after verebar (operative reason: his member was hurt and he feared entrusting it to the great gods); omitted the following elaboration (the quoted prayer to Priapus 'huic dixi...concolorque' and the closing couplet 'promisit fore...rogata fecit') which narrates the resulting vow and its fulfilment rather than the 'why'.

pairs.question: Velle quid hanc dicas, quamvis sim ligneus, hastam, oscula dat medio si qua puella mihi?
pairs.answer: Augure non opus est: 'in me' mihi credite, dixit 'utetur veris viribus hasta rudis.'
pairs.derivation: Author asks the reader what the wooden spear 'wants' when a girl kisses it, then answers himself that no augur is needed and reports what she said. Stripped section marker [XLIII]. Answer is the single reply sentence; the embedded quotation is part of the answering statement, not separate dialogue.

pairs.question: Quid frustra quereris, colone, mecum, quod quondam bene fructuosa malus autumnis sterilis duobus adstem?
pairs.answer: Non me praegravat, ut putas, senectus, nec sum grandine verberata dura, nec gemmas modo germine exeuntes seri frigoris ustulavit aura, nec venti pluviaeve siccitasve, quod de se quererer, malum dederunt; non sturnus mihi gracculusve raptor aut cornix anus aut aquosus anser aut corvos nocuit siticulosus: sed quod carmina pessimi poetae ramis sustineo laboriosis.
pairs.derivation: An apple-tree asks the farmer why he complains that it has stood barren two autumns (Quid...quereris...quod...sterilis...adstem?), then answers, ruling out the natural causes and ending with the real reason (sed quod carmina pessimi poetae ramis sustineo laboriosis). Stripped section marker [LXI]. Kept the full reply contiguous: the negations are an integral part of answering 'why barren', culminating in the operative sed-clause.
